title: Why Chronic Respiratory Disease Needs to Be a Global Health Priority
summary: Chronic respiratory diseases cause millions of deaths a year — most of them in countries with the least capacity to respond. Here's why that gap defines GALA Health's work.
body:
Chronic respiratory diseases — asthma, COPD, and related conditions — remain one of the most under-recognized categories of global disease burden. They cause close to 4 million deaths a year, and the impact falls disproportionately on low- and middle-income countries, where the vast majority of COPD deaths in people under 70 occur, according to the World Health Organization.

This is not primarily a medical gap. Effective prevention and treatment for chronic respiratory disease exist. What's missing, in most affected countries, is integration: national health systems that account for lung health in financing, diagnostics, and care pathways in the way they already do for other major disease categories.

GALA Health works to close that gap. Our approach is country-led, evidence-driven, and partnership-based — we provide technical assistance and policy advisory support to help governments build chronic respiratory disease care into the systems they already own, rather than proposing solutions built for them from the outside.

That includes work on prevention (indoor and outdoor air pollution, urban planning), access (diagnostics, essential medicines, insurance coverage), and a part of the picture too often left out of policy entirely: support for the informal caregivers who carry much of the daily burden of chronic respiratory disease at home.

What is not prioritized is not funded. What is not funded does not scale. Changing that is the work.
